findings.where: equiv/extract.py::enclosing; equiv/equiv.cpp::runStmt; P8-DISPATCHERS.md §5, concluding limits paragraph
findings.claim: The full indentation-chain comparison kills the round-2 outer-guard mutant, but it still does not prove reachability or complete control flow. A concrete surviving mutant is inserting `return;` immediately before the touch-start `if (!m_bDraggingThis) {`, at the same indentation as that if. All ten extracted statements and their recorded enclosing chains remain unchanged; the isolated statements still produce identical traces, although the actual touch handler no longer performs K4–K7. The detailed test description now acknowledges conditions outside the extracted lines, but the concluding assertion that the fake host proves guards and call order remains broader than the harness establishes. This is not a defect in the supplied product diff.
findings.evidence: `enclosing` records only preceding lines whose indentation is strictly lower than the current threshold. `runStmt` executes extracted statements in separate switch cases. The document acknowledges 'Isso não prova ... condições fora dessas linhas', but concludes 'ele prova argumentos, seleção de janela, guardas, ordem das chamadas'.

notes:
Approval is limited to incremental P8-A. No incorrect shipped replacement is demonstrated. The round-2 examples are addressed: the extractor now compares the full indentation chain, spawn error expectations include the actual normalized command, and unload wording no longer equates trivial destruction with module unload safety.

The supplied diff preserves K4–K8 and K10–K12 arguments, casts, focused-window selection, surrounding guards and source order. K5/K7 retain GOAL-relative parsing and missing-window rejection; K5 retains the translator's below-one guard, including NaN passing. The wrappers' booleans are ignored by callers, so ordinary reported failures do not short-circuit later actions. No deliberate plugin change to focus or minimization is visible.

ActionResult handling is explicit: success is unlogged, SILENT is intentionally unlogged, and other errors use the specified severity mapping and independent per-site gates. The revised integration oracle checks host messages, spawn commands and suppression summaries through the shipped wrapper. Ten fixed sites bound new plugin diagnostics to one line per site per ten-second window; pre-existing host logging is not bounded by this gate. Invalid-site failures are unlogged, but every supplied call uses a valid fixed site.

K11 still targets special:minimized silently on the focused window. Host workspace resolution/readiness, fallback focus and pointer-constraint differences remain documented, unresolved RDs requiring the deferred live tests. Unknown button strings still fall through without action or logging. Removing dispatchIfKnown bypasses third-party replacement/removal of its dispatcher names; that observable difference is correctly identified as a new RD requiring separate owner acceptance. This approval does not supply that acceptance.

The gate admits at the exact ten-second boundary, reports the accumulated suppression count and resets it on admission. Unsigned counter overflow wraps after 2^64 suppressed calls; near-maximum synthetic time-point addition can overflow the clock representation, but neither is demonstrated as a reachable operational defect here. Backward timestamps remain suppressed until the previous deadline; steady_clock does not move backward, and the synthetic test checks eventual reopening rather than immediate recovery. No multithreaded caller appears in the material; unsynchronized state relies on the stipulated event-loop execution.

The helpers add inline gate state and a static constexpr name table, but no registered callbacks, timers, retained host objects or asynchronous captures. No new post-unload execution path is shown. Physical dlclose/GNU-unique behavior is not established by trivial destruction and remains separate Q4 work.

The host-free suite includes shipped actionGate.hpp. NEW includes shipped hostActions.hpp and statements extracted from candidate barDeco.cpp. OLD uses baseline extracted statements and dispatchIfKnown plus the supplied translator bodies, with disclosed run-function renaming and map scaffolding. Host effects, selector behavior, parser behavior and workspace resolution are modeled, not executed against Hyprland. The real-header probe complements API coverage; the unmasked diagnostic comparison supports zero newly reported compilation errors, not a successful plugin build or link. The supplied build-comparison implementation is not included, so its results cannot be independently reconstructed from this material. The stale one-line logs samples do not illustrate the revised summary test, but the supplied runner, oracle and round-3 green log consistently check two lines. These limitations do not make this expressly incremental implementation insufficiently tested.
